built.summary:
U37a (the pure part) is written: one renderer used by both the officer's preview and the real send, plus suite sections §15 and §16. Nothing has been run. Under the hard rules I ran no node, tsx or tsc. I checked everything by reading it against the real types and call sites, so the first run of the suite will be the lead's.

**New file, src/lib/marketing/campaign-template.ts** (client-safe; imports only footer.ts and sms-compose.ts):
- Exports JINA = "{jina}", JINA_MAX_CHARS = 12 and CAMPAIGN_NAME_MAX_CHARS = 80.
- Types: CampaignDraftFields holds only what the officer types (name, bodySw, bodyEn, nameFallbackSw, nameFallbackEn). CampaignTemplate is those fields minus name, plus sourcePhrase. I used the column names from DECISIONS X12 (nameFallbackSw/En), not the spec's jinaFallback names.
- RecipientOrigin is "account" or "book". CampaignRecipient is { variant, name, token, origin }.
- Name rules (isUsableJina, isUsableFallback, jinaFor, firstNameFor): the name is folded to GSM-7 and only its first word is kept. Allowed characters are the Latin letters of the GSM-7 basic table, which are worked out from the table, not typed. An apostrophe or hyphen may appear inside a name, and an inner space only in the fallback. Length is 1 to 12, and a longer name is never cut short: it gets the fallback instead.
- Other pure pieces: worstCaseJina (12 W's), renderBody, scanPlaceholders (counts {jina}, names unknown tokens, counts stray braces), describeOffenders (invisible characters are labelled by code point, e.g. "U+00A0 no-break space", with a foldable flag) and variantFor (follows OD42; a ZH reader gets Swahili).
- counterFor(body, variant, fallback, sourcePhrase): sizes the body with the 12-letter worst-case name, the source phrase and the footer, through composeMarketing. It returns segments, units, bodyUnits, budget, left, footerUnits, sourceUnits, jinaReserve, offenders, problems, fallbackProblems and ok.
- validateCampaignTemplate(f, sourcePhrase): Swahili is required; English is optional but fully checked when present; the name is 1 to 80 characters; the source line has its own rules.
- renderForRecipient(t, r): the one renderer for each recipient. Three rules are enforced here so callers don't have to:
  - A book contact always gets the fallback name, even if a caller passes a name in (recycled numbers).
  - The source phrase is printed for every recipient whose origin is not exactly "account" (M5: priced in, never dropped).
  - The result is refused if the stored template would fail validation.
- Per M5, the counter always prices a non-blank phrase. So a players-only campaign keeps room it does not use: that costs characters, never money.

**Defect found and fixed in footer.ts (🔴 in the comment):** composeMarketing put the source phrase in front of the body.
- The "must begin with 50pick" check then read the phrase, so any phrase not itself starting with "50pick" (§10's fixture "Umetupa namba yako 50pick." is one) would refuse every message carrying it.
- The over-cap sentence also counted the phrase as the officer's own text against a budget that had already taken it out.
- Nothing passed a phrase yet, so nothing shipped wrong. The phrase now sits between the body and the footer, matching OQ3's safe default ("the footer carries it"), with the same size cost.
- operatorBudget now trims the phrase before testing whether it is empty, and composeMarketing's doc names its one caller.

**Suite additions in campaign-compose.test.mts:** existing sections are untouched. The new sections run in their own functions (checkTemplate, checkOneComposer), so check(naiveDivide) still breaks exactly one assertion.
- §15.0–§15.12 hold 33 assertions:
  - §15.1: {jina} reserves 12 septets.
  - §15.2: every real message fits inside what the counter said, over 42 written-out names × 2 templates × 2 languages × 2 origins.
  - §15.3–§15.8 follow the spec.
  - §15.9 (M5): the counter prices the phrase; a book message carries it just before the footer and still starts with 50pick; an unknown origin carries it.
  - §15.10: recycled numbers.
  - §15.11: rules for the source line.
  - §15.12: the campaign name.
- §16.1 checks that composeMarketing( is called only from campaign-template.ts, across the whole src population (srcFiles() plus decomment).
- §16.6 checks that campaign-template.ts imports no server module, and that it is in client-graph-safe's PINNED list.
- --prove-red has 20 new in-memory plants, each required to fail its matching assertion: P1–P8 from the spec, plus plants for OD42, M5 (three), recycled numbers, firstNameFor, the source line, the name, and two §16 plants. No files are written.

**§16.6 will be RED until the lead pins the file:** scripts/client-graph-safe.test.mjs was off-limits to me, so campaign-template.ts is not yet in its PINNED list. Both the §16.6 assertion and the red baseline fail until that pin lands; the snippet is in How to verify step 1.

No package.json keys are needed (test:campaign-compose is already in predeploy) and no section module was created.
howToVerify: 1. Before any run, add the pin to scripts/client-graph-safe.test.mjs PINNED, after "lib/marketing/footer.ts": a comment `// ⭐ ADDED 2026-10-01 (U37a). THE ONE campaign renderer: the composer client's counter imports it; the test send and U43 render through it on the server. It imports only footer.ts and sms-compose.ts.` followed by the entry `"lib/marketing/campaign-template.ts",`. Without it, §16.6 ⭐ and the red §0 baseline stay RED by design.

2. `rm -rf .next` is not needed (no route). Run serially through the lock: `~/heavy-node-lock.sh run <who> npm run typecheck`. campaign-template.ts and footer.ts are in tsc's include; the .mts suite is not, but it is written to be type-correct.

3. `~/heavy-node-lock.sh run <who> npm run test:campaign-compose`. Expect every §1–§14 line unchanged and green, then §15.0–§15.12 and §16.1/§16.6 green. The §16.1 log line should print about 1,222 src files walked, and composeMarketing named only in src/lib/marketing/footer.ts and src/lib/marketing/campaign-template.ts.

4. `~/heavy-node-lock.sh run <who> npm run red:campaign-compose`. Expect §0 baseline ok, every existing plant still firing, 17 new §15 plants and 3 §16 plants each showing PLANT LANDED plus `└─ fires` for every expected regex (P2 must fire §15.1 ⭐, §15.1 ⛔ and §15.2 ⭐; P3 must fire §15.2 ⭐ and §15.3 ⭐ the renderer), and the final §4b finding still `only assertion the division defect breaks` = 1.
5. `~/heavy-node-lock.sh run <who> npm run test:client-graph-safe`: the new pin must walk clean (footer → app-url, support-config, sms-compose).

6. Optional: `git diff src/lib/marketing/footer.ts` shows the only behaviour change is where the source phrase goes and the over-cap 'this uses N' counting the officer's text alone. With no phrase (every existing caller and test), the output is byte-identical.
openQuestions: Docs (I may not edit them). The lead should update docs/MARKETING-CAMPAIGN-AND-CONTACTS-SETUP.md: (a) §9 U37 text: U37a shipped, with per-variant nameFallbackSw/En, worst-case sizing (12 reserved), the source phrase priced in, and book contacts always getting the fallback. (b) The OQ3 row (line ~1104) says the phrase is 'counted with its trailing space'. It now sits between the body and the footer, counted with the one space before it. (c) §0h: record the delegated calls (name only from the player's own account; one fallback per language; ZH gets Swahili; the phrase always priced; renderer refuses an invalid stored template).

Source phrase wording and population gate (G5/OQ3). The renderer prints SmsCampaign.sourcePhrase for every non-account recipient, but nothing supplies the wording yet, and inventing a Swahili sentence is forbidden. While the phrase is blank, a campaign reaching book contacts would go out without one. U38/U40 (or U37b) must decide whether to refuse confirming a population that includes book contacts while sourcePhrase is blank.

API differences from the U37 spec that U37b/U43 must use: validateCampaignTemplate(f, sourcePhrase) takes the phrase as a required second argument. CampaignDraftFields has no sourcePhrase, so an officer cannot post one. counterFor(body, variant, fallback, sourcePhrase) has a required 4th argument. CampaignRecipient carries origin: 'account' | 'book'. VariantCounter adds sourceUnits and fallbackProblems. U37b's saveCampaignDraft should feed the server-side phrase and store counters.SW/EN encoding+segments as codingSw/segmentsSw/codingEn/segmentsEn (X12/X15).

composeMarketing's UCS-2 refusal sentence still quotes the raw character, which is blank for a no-break space. The composer screen (U37b) should show VariantCounter.offenders[].label (code-point labels) for the 'Forced to Unicode by' line, rather than relying on that sentence. Alternatively, a later footer.ts edit could reuse describeOffenders.

The footer.ts change moves the source phrase after the body, per OQ3's safe default ('the footer carries a short source phrase'). If the lawyer's OQ3 answer requires the phrase at the very start, only composeMarketing's text line changes; units and budget are placement-independent.

findings.problem: DECISIONS M5 says the source phrase is 'priced in, never dropped' for every recipient whose number did not come from their own account, and the module's own header calls a dropped phrase 'the unlawful direction'. The code does not do this. renderForRecipient sets `phrase = fromAccount ? "" : (t.sourcePhrase ?? "").trim()`, and while SmsCampaign.sourcePhrase is blank (the state until owner gate G5 supplies the wording) a book contact or an unknown origin renders with no source line and `ok: true`. U43 is meant to trust this renderer's `ok`, so book contacts would be sent messages with no ETA s.31(c) source statement and nothing would refuse them. The engineer listed this as an open question for U38/U40, but the renderer is the single choke point and its doc says it enforces such rules 'so no caller has to remember it'. No assertion covers it: §15.2 even requires `r.ok` for origin "book" on the template that has no phrase.
findings.fix: In renderForRecipient: when `!fromAccount` and the trimmed phrase is blank, push a refusal such as "This number came from the contact book and the campaign has no source line yet (OQ3, owner gate G5), so it cannot be sent." Change §15.2 so the no-phrase template renders only origin "account" (or expects the refusal for "book"). Add a §15.9 assertion that a blank phrase refuses a book recipient and an unknown origin while an account recipient still renders ok, plus a red plant that removes the refusal. To make 'priced in' true before the wording exists, consider a SOURCE_PHRASE_MAX_CHARS constant that counterFor reserves when the phrase is blank (the same approach as worstCaseJina).

findings.problem: The doc comment (and the report's third 'enforced' rule) says the renderer refuses whenever the stored template could not have passed validateCampaignTemplate, 'a bad source line' included. It does not, in two cases. (a) It never runs the worst-case counter. A stored body whose worst case is over the cap by k septets, with k up to 6 when the fallback is 'Rafiki', renders ok:true for every book contact and every short-named account, and is refused only for long names. The result is a partial send of a template that validate refuses. (b) sourcePhraseProblems runs on `phrase`, which is "" for account recipients, so a stored phrase like 'Source {jina}' or a UCS-2 phrase renders ok:true for every account recipient and is refused for book recipients. Validate also checks the untrimmed phrase while the renderer checks the trimmed one, so 'x\n' fails validate and passes the renderer. No §15 assertion or red plant covers this refusal rule at all, so the claimed rule has nothing that can fail.
findings.fix: In renderForRecipient, add `counterFor(body, variant, fallback, t.sourcePhrase ?? "").problems`, its fallbackProblems, and `sourcePhraseProblems(t.sourcePhrase ?? "")` (untrimmed, whatever the origin) to `problems`. That gives the renderer exactly validate's per-variant verdict and makes the doc true. Add a §15.13 asserting that a stored template that is 3 over in the worst case, one with two {jina}, and one with a braced source line are each refused for BOTH an account and a book recipient. Add a plant that drops the template re-check and must fire it.

findings.problem: footer.ts is outside U37a's declared file set. The spec lists campaign-template.ts and the suite, and the critic's group P1 gives U37a 'no shared src file'. The edit also changes behaviour in a live module. It moves the source phrase from before the body to between the body and the footer, and changes the over-cap sentence's 'this uses N'. The fix is sound: the old placement refused any phrase that did not start with '50pick'. But placement is OQ3's subject (owner gate G5). The OQ3 safe default reads 'the footer carries a short source phrase', and the new placement puts the phrase at the end of the officer's body line, before the footer's newline, not inside the footer. The change appears in the report but in no decision.
findings.fix: The lead should explicitly accept the footer.ts edit and record it as a delegated call in §0h, with the OQ3 row (~line 1109) updated to say where the phrase now sits ('counted with the one space before it'). Alternatively, place the phrase after the footer's leading newline so 'the footer carries it' is literally true. The size is identical either way. Also confirm that no concurrent unit is editing footer.ts before this commit lands.

findings.problem: sourcePhraseProblems has no length limit. A long phrase from the server (for example 120 characters) produces no sourcePhrase problem. Instead every body gets the over-cap refusal with a negative room ('you have -40 characters before the required footer'), blamed on the officer's body, which the officer cannot fix. Without a maximum, the counter also cannot reserve a bound for the phrase before G5 supplies the wording.
findings.fix: Export a SOURCE_PHRASE_MAX_CHARS (in septets) and refuse a longer phrase on the sourcePhrase field. Use the same constant as the counter's reserve while the phrase is blank (see the high finding). Add an assertion to §15.11 and a plant that removes the limit.

findings.problem: The 'left is budget − bodyUnits' half of the second §15.6 assertion is true by construction: counterFor computes `left: composed.budget - bodyUnits`. It cannot fail against the real code, and no plant targets it. Only the `footerUnits === 49` part can actually fail.
findings.fix: Compare `left` with a value worked out independently, e.g. `operatorBudget("SW", PHRASE) - unitsIn(worstTyped(t6.bodySw).trim(), "GSM7")`. Add a plant (a counter whose left ignores the reserve or the phrase) that must fire it.

findings.problem: §16.6 ⭐ and the red §0 baseline, plus the 'left out of PINNED' plant's PLANT LANDED line, stay RED until `"lib/marketing/campaign-template.ts"` is added to client-graph-safe's PINNED list. That file is off-limits to U37a and is being edited by other units right now. test:campaign-compose is already in predeploy, so committing U37a without the pin in the same commit breaks predeploy.
findings.fix: The lead must add the pin (with its ⭐ ADDED comment, after "lib/marketing/footer.ts") in the SAME commit as U37a, written exactly with double quotes so TEMPLATE_PIN matches. Then run test:campaign-compose, red:campaign-compose and test:client-graph-safe one after another through the heavy lock.

review.verdict:
The U37a code is mostly sound, but it should not ship as it stands. Read against the real sms-compose.ts and footer.ts types, I found no TypeScript errors. Nothing imports a server module, the new files contain no raw zero-width or other invisible characters, and none of the 'never edit' files were touched. I traced every §15 and §16 assertion by hand against the real code and each one passes. All 20 new red plants land and fire the assertion they are matched to; P2 fires §15.1 ⭐, §15.1 ⛔ and §15.2 ⭐, and P3 fires §15.2 ⭐ and §15.3 ⭐. check(naiveDivide) still breaks exactly one assertion, and §10, §11 and §13 are unchanged without a phrase. The name rules, the 12-letter worst-case sizing, the fold, OD42 and the X12 column names all match the decisions.

Two real problems remain. (1) HIGH, DECISIONS M5: while sourcePhrase is blank, renderForRecipient renders book and unknown-origin recipients with ok:true and no source line, which is the 'dropped' outcome M5 forbids, and no assertion catches it. (2) MEDIUM: the renderer claims it refuses any stored template that validate would refuse, but it skips the worst-case check and skips the source-line check for account recipients. That allows a partial send, and nothing tests the refusal rule.

There are four smaller points. footer.ts was edited outside U37a's file set; the change is sound but it is an OQ3 placement call that needs recording. The source phrase has no length limit. One half of a §15.6 assertion is always true. §16.6 needs the client-graph-safe pin in the same commit, or predeploy goes red.
